doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Moving to LSU: G.I. Bill, short stories and Faulkner
summary: An English teacher got him into LSU; Audre recalls weekly short stories and Allison's glimpses of William Faulkner.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Then you go back to U-Miss and you go for your degree... Did you get your degree there?
No, I didn’t get a degree...
Oh, you transferred to LSU, excuse me. What brought you from Oxford, Mississippi to Baton Rouge?
Well, uh...
We got married. He had started playing around in Louisiana and different places...
I went to LSU, and I remember applying to LSU... An English teacher got me into LSU.
I guess you had the G.I. Bill, too.
Yes, I had the G.I. Bill.
He wrote terrific short stories. Really good ones.
I don’t remember that
Do they still exist?

Yeah. Somewhere they’re still... We never threw them away. I remember that we had a little apartment, and you had a short story due every Monday, and I was always like amazed... Because I like to write. He would sit down with a pencil Sunday night and write the story.
I don’t know...
Then your English teacher wanted you to get an agent in New Orleans, but you said no, you were going to do music instead.
I don’t know... [LAUGHS]
Do you remember some of the writers you liked then?
No. I didn’t know about William Faulkner at that time...
Yes... Mose, I hate to keep interrupting you, but you met William Faulkner at Ole Miss...
Yes. I met him later.
Oh, after we were married and we went back. I thought... You used to tell me stories about how they called him “Count No-Count,” when he’d be hanging around the town.

Yeah. They used to call him that. He started out working at fuel consumption something...I don’t know...at the University of Mississippi... I don’t know anything about him. I used to see him sometimes at the beer place.
